newsitem.title: JAPAN: NCB says to leave Jan prime rate unchanged.
newsitem.headline: NCB says to leave Jan prime rate unchanged.

text.p: Nippon Credit Bank Ltd (NCB) said on Thursday it would leave its long-term prime lending rate for January unchanged at a record low 2.5 percent.
NCB also said it would leave the coupon rate on its January five-year debentures, sold to institutional investors, unchanged at 2.15 percent.
NCB left the coupon unchanged despite a sharp deviation between the December debenture coupon and its secondary market yield.
The prime rate is applied to loans of one year and longer to the long-term credit bank's most creditworthy clients.
NCB's December debenture was trading at a yield of around 3.06 or 3.07 percent in the secondary market on Wednesday, about 90 basis points above its coupon.
The Industrial Bank of Japan Ltd (IBJ), the largest of Japan's three long-term credit banks, said on Wednesday it would leave its long-term prime lending rate for January unchanged at 2.5 percent.
